scope: Runner input, source-closure and runtime-identity hardening only; not owner approval, private-pack review, benchmark evidence, baseline seal or A9 closure.

rejection_rounds.finding: Nested directory symlinks were not traversed or rejected by the Python-only source glob.
Credential names could override PATH, Python, loader, locale and other execution-control environment.

findings: Unchecked bytecode and native extension artifacts were importable but outside the source hash.
Ambient PATH was unbound and could change runner interpreter selection.

rejection_rounds.finding: Using os.defpath alone selected the host system Python rather than the locked backend environment.
The python3 entry selected by the child PATH could be retargeted independently from sys.executable without changing admission identity.

limitations: The review assumes a trusted local operator and does not claim cryptographic protection against a malicious same-user filesystem race.
No provider, database or remote operation was performed.
Technical subagent approval cannot replace owner review or human authorization.
